I just gave my a Grokbot four years of past tax returns and financial files.  Just a dump of folders and unlabled files.

K-1s, 1099s, mortgage statements, HSA records, and every email with our CPA.  266 files.

I just said, please double check my CPA's work.

A few minutes later, it had found a lot of mistakes.

Mortgage interest left off our 2022 return entirely.

HSA payroll contributions counted twice, four years in a row, which created a penalty tax that never should have existed.

A missing IRA form for Jen that would have cost us.

On this year's return: home office errors, two K-1s missing, an outdated 1099, and startup losses we never claimed.

And a retirement contribution the return already deducted...that we hadn't actually deposited.  

I sent it all to our CPA.  They sent back an amended return.  The bot reviewed that too.

One fix went the wrong direction.  The explanation had typos.

Three versions later, all in one afternoon, it said ready to sign.

Just a few hours start to finish.  With about 90 seconds of my time and attention required. I was just the meat proxy hitting send as Grokbot watched the replies in my email.  

Our CPA is great and turned every fix around the same day.  

We chatted afterwards.  He wanted to know what I was using - just normal ole' grokbot.

I asked him what he was using?  No AI tools.  

I set him up with @magnetictax for next season (we're an investor).  All CPAs should be using Magnetic Tax or something like it.  Every single one.

All individuals should be double checking the work and past work with Grokbot or something like that.  

Want to copy the exact the prompt I used?  it was just this:

"Please do a thorough review of my taxes and help me understand if my CPA made any mistakes"

"Think deeply"

Or just tag your bot into this thread.

note_tweet.text:
Lunar Surface Robotics (Moon)

Rocket Lab supported @FireflySpace's Blue Ghost lunar lander with our MAX Flight and MAX Ground Data Software suites, alongside trajectory design and backup mission operations support.

We also provided the high-efficiency solar panels that powered the Blue Ghost spacecraft that successfully landed on the Mare Cirsium on the lunar surface.

Motiv Space Systems (now Rocket Lab Robotics) also developed the lightweight chassis, mobility actuators, and motor control electronics for @NASA's CADRE autonomous lunar rovers. Currently, we are developing a single-axis scanning gimbal with integrated avionics for the EMILIA-3D PRISM payload, an instrument designed to produce high-resolution 3D thermal maps of the Moon.

Solar Power on the Red Planet: Ingenuity, InSight, and Perseverance (Mars)

SolAero, acquired by Rocket Lab in 2022, has powered several landmark Mars exploration missions, including:

- Ingenuity Mars Helicopter: Powered by our solar panel — populated with ultra-lightweight, 33% efficient Inverted Metamorphic Multijunction (IMM) solar cells — mounted atop its rotor blades.

- InSight Lander: Our high-efficiency solar panels powered Northrop Grumman's UltraFlex solar arrays in support of the lander's seismic operations on the Martian surface.

- Mars 2020 Cruise Stage: Our solar panels kept Perseverance powered and healthy during its months-long transit to Mars.

GRAIL & LADEE (Moon)

Motorized Lightband (MLB) separation technology from Planetary Systems Corporation, acquired by Rocket Lab in 2021, supported @NASA's GRAIL and LADEE lunar missions.

These flight-proven, non-pyrotechnic mechanisms provide controlled, low-shock separation between spacecraft and launch-vehicle elements to safeguard delicate science instruments.

Martian Surface Robotics: Perseverance (Mars)

Rocket Lab Robotics hardware is actively operating on Mars aboard NASA’s Perseverance rover.

Motiv Space Systems, acquired by Rocket Lab this year, designed and built Perseverance’s primary 2-meter, 5-joint robotic arm that positions coring tools directly against Martian rock faces using a 6-DOF force-torque sensor for sampling, and delivered the opto-mechanical system inclusive of zoom, focus, and filter-wheel for the Mastcam-Z science cameras.

Artemis (Moon)

Under contract with @LockheedMartin, thousands of Rocket Lab’s high-efficiency space-grade solar cell assemblies have powered, or will power, all of the Orion spacecraft for the @NASAArtemis missions. Our cells are integrated into Orion’s four European Service Module solar array wings.

Rocket Lab technology also deployed the secondary deep space payloads on Artemis I: our Canisterized Satellite Dispensers (CSDs), developed by Planetary Systems Corporation, were installed inside the SLS Orion Stage Adapter to cleanly eject 6U CubeSats into lunar and deep-space trajectories.

🌕 September’s Full Harvest Moon is lighting up the night sky tonight!

Unlike many traditional Full Moon names, the Harvest Moon isn’t tied to a specific month. It’s the name given to the Full Moon that falls closest to the September equinox. This year, that’s September’s Moon.

Around the timing of the Harvest Moon, the Moon rises at roughly the same time for several evenings in a row across much of the Northern Hemisphere. Historically, this meant more moonlight shortly after sunset, giving farmers additional light to gather crops during the busy harvest season. 🌾

If skies are clear where you are, take a moment to look up and enjoy September’s Harvest Moon tonight. ✨
